## The Clients

**Ideal client profile:**
- Technology companies and their investors
- Life sciences companies and their investors
- FinTech and AI companies (also served per Chambers profile)
- Middle-market transactions
- Both public and private acquirers
- Venture-backed startups, large-cap technology companies, venture capital
  funds, and international corporations purchasing U.S. assets

**Notable representative clients (M&A):**
- Buy-side: Oracle, Dell, eBay, Applied Materials, Disney, Alibaba, Adobe,
  Gilead Sciences
- Sell-side / counterparties: Dropbox, Twitter, Samsung, Apple, Roche,
  Zimmer Biomet

**Primary problems clients come to BSV to solve:**
- Complex M&A transactions (both domestic and cross-border)
- Tax structuring for transactions, including tax-free reorganizations
- IP and technology transactions, licensing, and strategy
- Corporate finance and governance matters

**Client fears / objections (what they worry about before hiring outside
counsel):**
- Whether the firm has the right **competence** for the specific matter
- Whether the firm has the right **experience** with similar transactions
- Whether the firm will be **responsive** when the deal needs to move fast

These three concerns drive everything. The new site copy should signal
competence, depth of experience, and responsiveness on every page —
not as abstract claims but with proof (deal experience, partner access,
testimonials).

**How clients currently find the firm:**
- Attorney referrals (from other lawyers / co-counsel)
- Client referrals (past clients)

**What clients value about working with BSV (recurring themes from
testimonials):**
- **Responsiveness** — "always responsive," "available for questions at
  all times," "moved heaven and earth"
- **Pragmatism** — "highly efficient, pragmatic and easy to work with,"
  "well organized"
- **Cost-effectiveness** — efficient billing, often delivering under budget
- **Direct partner access** — clients work with named partners, not handed
  off to junior associates
- **Deep tech M&A expertise** — knowledge of market standards

Representative quote: *"BSV was my rock throughout the $6 billion merger
between Athelas and Commure."* — Daniel Brian, GC, Commure, Inc.

## Positioning

**Fee structure:** Hourly billing, paired with an **estimate of total cost**
for each engagement. The new site should be transparent about this —
prospective clients should not be left guessing about how the firm bills.

**Key differentiator (lead message for new site):**
> Team work to get good results.

The firm distinguishes itself from larger firms by giving every matter the
attention and priority of a boutique, and from generalist boutiques by
specializing in M&A and technology transactions. For matters requiring
outside expertise (e.g., antitrust), BSV curates "a team of elite
specialists" rather than over-claiming in-house capability.

**Tone and personality:**
- Existing site reads: professional, direct, business-focused, concise,
  credentials-forward
- For the new site: keep the underlying professionalism and substance,
  but warm it up. Aim for "modern, approachable, expert" — see Design
  Direction below.

## Design Direction

### Visual references (provided by Jon)

**1. Strix Law — https://www.strixlaw.com**
- Clean, modern, sans-serif typography
- Minimalist layout with generous whitespace
- Imagery that mixes professional credibility with approachable warmth
  (stylized photos + illustrated landscape elements)
- Conversational copy that distances from stuffy BigLaw aesthetic
- Layered background imagery creating subtle visual depth
- Signals nimbleness and partnership, not institutional distance
- Personality: **approachable, founder-friendly, warm**

**2. Norm Law — https://www.normlaw.com**
- Stark, premium minimalist scheme (black text on white)
- Sans-serif typography; large, bold headlines with strong hierarchy
- Restrained imagery — professional headshots, no illustrations or
  decorative graphics
- Generous whitespace; sophisticated layout
- Copy is direct and confident — institutional gravitas
- AI-native positioning, targeting investment funds, private equity, VC,
  and real estate clients
- Personality: **premium, forward-thinking, institutionally credible**

### What both references share (the BSV design DNA)

These are the design principles that should govern the new site:
- **Modern sans-serif typography** — no traditional law-firm serifs
- **Generous whitespace** — breathing room over dense content blocks
- **Strong typographic hierarchy** — large, confident headlines do the
  heavy lifting
- **Restraint over ornament** — no clutter, no stock-photo theatrics
- **Distance from BigLaw aesthetic** — neither site looks like a 1990s
  partnership website

### What they differ on, and what BSV should choose

| Dimension | Strix | Norm | BSV target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warmth | Approachable, conversational | Premium, institutional | **Premium, but warmer than Norm — BSV serves both tech founders and large public companies, so it can't be too cold** |
| Imagery | Illustrated landscapes + photos | Photos only, restrained | **Mix — restrained overall, but with selective creative graphics (see "creative art" goal below)** |
| Color | Neutral + blue accents + nature tones | Black & white minimalism | **TBD; lean modern minimal with a single confident accent color** |

### Stated goals (from intake)

- **"Update it to look more new"** — modernize away from the current
  bsvlaw.com traditional look
- **"Have some creative art"** — incorporate illustration, abstract
  graphics, or other distinctive visual elements (not just stock photos)

### Note on "creative art" given the references

There's a slight tension between (a) wanting "creative art" and (b) liking
Norm Law, which has essentially no decorative graphics. The right move is
probably: **restrained, premium foundation (Norm-style) with one or two
distinctive visual moments** — e.g., a custom abstract hero graphic, a
stylized practice-area icon set, or a subtle illustrated motif used
sparingly. Not a fully illustrated site (Strix-style). The design phase
will propose specific options.

### Color direction

Not yet decided. Will be developed during the design phase. The current
site uses navy and white; we're open to keeping that lineage or going in
a fresh direction. Given the two references favor monochrome + restraint,
recommend exploring: (a) deep navy + warm white + single accent, or
(b) near-black + white with a confident accent. Final decision deferred
to design phase.

### Headshots

None ready. All attorney photos for the new site need to be taken. The
build can proceed with placeholders; final photos will be swapped in
before launch.

## Security & Compliance Requirements

*These are non-negotiable for a law firm website. GSD must include a dedicated
security phase in the project plan to address each of these before launch.*

- **HTTP security headers** — configured in `vercel.json`: Content-Security-Policy,
  X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy
- **Secrets management** — all API keys stored as Vercel environment variables only;
  never hardcoded in source files or committed to git
- **Git hygiene** — `.env` and `.env.local` files excluded from git via `.gitignore`
- **Supabase Row Level Security** — RLS enabled on all database tables (including leads)
- **Server-side input validation** — contact form validated on the server, not just
  the browser; malformed submissions rejected before reaching the database
- **Spam protection** — honeypot field on the contact form at minimum; rate limiting
  recommended for production
- **No sensitive data in built output** — verify the compiled `dist/` folder contains
  no API keys, service keys, or credentials
- **ABA Formal Opinion 477R compliance** — attorneys have a professional responsibility
  to protect the confidentiality of client communications, including pre-engagement
  inquiries submitted via web forms; the contact form, data storage, and notification
  system must meet this standard
- **Pre-launch security audit** — run `/hc-firm-site:check` before going live; the
  Security section of that audit must fully pass
